traditions/the-pentecostal-mission/summa: Founded in Colombo, Ceylon, in 1923 by Pastor Paul (born Ramankutty, a Keralite convert from Hinduism) with Alwin R. de Alwis, and known first as the Ceylon Pentecostal Mission. Its international headquarters is now at Irumbuliyur near Tambaram, Chennai. It is an indigenous South Asian Pentecostal church best known for its celibate, propertyless ministers who live in communal 'faith homes' and dress entirely in white.
traditions/the-pentecostal-mission/disti: Full-time ministers, men and women, are celibate, hold no private property and live together in faith homes
Ministers and worshippers wear white; jewellery and ornaments are renounced
Strong emphasis on divine healing, with ministers declining medical treatment
Teaching that sanctified 'overcomers' will form the company of Mount Zion (Revelation 14)
Large annual conventions, including the international convention in Chennai
Congregations known in different countries as CPM, TPM, Zion Pentecostal Mission or New Testament Church
traditions/the-pentecostal-mission/profi: Scripture, read in a holiness-Pentecostal way, with great weight on the instruction of the senior ministers.
Salvation by grace through repentance and faith, followed by water baptism, sanctification and Baptism in the Holy Spirit evidenced by tongues; a life of separation from the world is stressed.
Baptism of believers by immersion and the Lord's Supper; footwashing is practised in some settings.
Premillennial; the faithful and sanctified are taught to await the rapture and a place with Christ in Zion.
A centralised ministry under a chief pastor and senior ministers; local faith homes direct the congregations.
Simple Pentecostal services with congregational singing, testimony and prayer; worshippers sit on the floor and dress in white.
traditions/believers-eastern-church/summ: An episcopal church that grew out of the Gospel for Asia (now GFA World) mission founded by K. P. Yohannan of Niranam, Kerala, in 1979. Organised as Believers Church in 1993, it adopted episcopal government in 2003 with Yohannan as first Metropolitan, and took the name Believers Eastern Church in 2017 to express affinity with the ancient Eastern churches. Headquartered in Thiruvalla, Kerala, it combines evangelical teaching with Eastern-style vestments, liturgy and titles. After Yohannan's death in 2024, Samuel Mor Theophilus was elected Metropolitan.
traditions/believers-eastern-church/dist: Evangelical doctrine within an Eastern-style episcopal and liturgical form
Grew from the Gospel for Asia mission's support of native missionaries
Strong rural mission work across North India, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Myanmar
Runs Believers Church Medical College Hospital and schools in Thiruvalla
Has faced public scrutiny over GFA finances in the United States and India
traditions/believers-eastern-church/prof: Scripture as the final authority, received within what the church calls the ancient apostolic and Eastern tradition.
Salvation by grace through personal faith in Christ, with a strong call to evangelism.
Baptism and the Holy Qurbana (Eucharist) celebrated with an Eastern-style liturgy.
Expectation of Christ's return; not a central point of controversy.
Episcopal: a Metropolitan and bishops with a synod, organised into dioceses.
Liturgical worship in Malayalam, Hindi and other languages, with vestments and Eastern titles.
traditions/st-thomas-evangelical-church/: St. Thomas Evangelical Church of India

An evangelical episcopal church in Kerala that separated from the Mar Thoma Syrian Church on 26 January 1961, after a long dispute and lawsuit in which lay leader K. N. Daniel accused the Mar Thoma leadership of drifting back towards Jacobite (Syriac Orthodox) doctrine and practice. The courts ruled against Daniel, the Supreme Court giving final judgement in 1965. Headquartered at Manjadi, Thiruvalla, it keeps a reformed Malankara heritage with a stronger evangelical emphasis.
Separated from the Mar Thoma Church in 1961 over the purity of its reformation
Episcopal government with a presiding bishop
Evangelical preaching, revival conventions and missionary work
Shares the Malayalam reformed-Syrian heritage of the Mar Thoma Church
Scripture as the sole rule of faith, as the Mar Thoma reformers of the nineteenth century had urged.
Salvation by grace through faith in Christ; personal conversion and assurance are emphasised.
Baptism and the Lord's Supper as the two sacraments of the Gospel.
Episcopal, with bishops, clergy and an elected representative assembly.
Malayalam liturgy derived from the reformed Mar Thoma order, with evangelical hymnody and preaching.
traditions/tamil-evangelical-lutheran-ch: The church of Tamil Nadu that descends from the first Protestant mission in India, begun at Tranquebar (Tharangambadi) in 1706 by Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg and Heinrich Plütschau of the Danish-Halle Mission, and later continued by the Leipzig Mission. It was constituted as an autonomous church in 1919, with headquarters at Tiruchirappalli; its first Indian bishop, Rajah B. Manikam, was consecrated in 1956.
Heir of Ziegenbalg's Tranquebar mission, the first Protestant mission in India (1706)
Episcopal Lutheran church holding the Augsburg Confession and Luther's Small Catechism
Tamil Bible and hymn tradition reaching back to Ziegenbalg and Vedanayagam Sastri
Schools, hospitals and the Gurukul Lutheran Theological College tradition
Scripture as the norm, with the Lutheran Confessions as its faithful exposition.
Justification by grace through faith alone, for Christ's sake.
Baptism (including infants) and the Lord's Supper, in which Christ's body and blood are truly present.
Christ's return to judge the living and the dead.
Episcopal: a bishop with a church council and synod, headquartered in Tiruchirappalli.
Lutheran liturgy in Tamil with Tamil lyrics (keerthanai) alongside translated chorales.
traditions/andhra-evangelical-lutheran-c: The largest Lutheran church in India, based in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh. It grew from the mission begun on 31 July 1842 by John Christian Frederick ('Father') Heyer of the Lutheran General Synod in America, and was constituted as a self-governing church in 1927. Its growth came largely through Dalit (Mala and Madiga) mass movements in the coastal Andhra delta.
Founded on Father Heyer's 1842 mission in Guntur
Largest Lutheran church in India, with Telugu-speaking membership
Grew through Dalit group conversions in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries
Andhra Christian College, hospitals and schools in Guntur and Rajahmundry
Infant baptism and the Lord's Supper with real presence.
Return of Christ and final judgement.
Episcopal: a bishop with a church council, synods and districts.
traditions/indian-brethren/summary: Autonomous Open Brethren assemblies in India. Anthony Norris Groves brought Brethren principles to India from 1833, and his disciple John Arulappan spread them among Tamils; in Kerala the movement is dated to March 1899, when four men broke bread without a priest at Kumbanad after the preaching of the English evangelist J. G. Gregson. The German missionary Volbrecht Nagel, formerly of the Basel Mission, became its leading pioneer, and many early members came from Mar Thoma and other Syrian Christian families.
traditions/indian-brethren/distinctives/: No ordained clergy; weekly 'breaking of bread' led by the brothers
Each assembly autonomous, with no central governing body
Believer's baptism by immersion and strong lay preaching
Large gospel conventions, notably at Kumbanad
Women veil their heads and do not speak in the assembly meeting
traditions/indian-brethren/profile/autho: Scripture alone, read with a literal and dispensational hermeneutic.
traditions/indian-brethren/profile/salva: Salvation by grace through faith; assurance of salvation stressed.
traditions/indian-brethren/profile/sacra: Believer's baptism by immersion and the weekly Lord's Supper as a memorial.
traditions/indian-brethren/profile/escha: Dispensational premillennialism with a pre-tribulation rapture.
traditions/indian-brethren/profile/gover: Congregational: each assembly led by recognised elders.
traditions/indian-brethren/profile/worsh: Unstructured worship meetings with open participation by men; Malayalam hymnody (e.g. K. V. Simon).
traditions/sharon-fellowship-church/summ: An indigenous Pentecostal church founded in 1953 at Thiruvalla, Kerala, by Pastor P. J. Thomas (1914–1998), who had studied at Serampore and Wheaton College, together with T. G. Koshy and ten others. It grew from the Sharon Bible School on property Thomas bought in March 1953 and is known for combining Pentecostal piety with an emphasis on theological education.
traditions/sharon-fellowship-church/dist: Indigenous Kerala Pentecostal church with Indian leadership from the start
Emphasis on trained ministry through Sharon Bible College
Linked with the founding of Faith Theological Seminary, Manakala
Classical Pentecostal theology with relatively moderate dress rules
traditions/sharon-fellowship-church/prof: Salvation by grace through faith; Spirit baptism with speaking in tongues as a subsequent experience.
Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper.
General council with regional centres and local pastors.
Pentecostal worship in Malayalam and other languages.
traditions/church-of-god-full-gospel-ind: Church of God (Full Gospel) in India

The Indian branch of the Church of God (Cleveland, Tennessee), headquartered at Mulakuzha near Chengannur, Kerala. It began with the American missionary Robert F. Cook, who reached India in 1913, moved his work to Kerala and by 1923 had founded some 36 congregations; his work joined the Church of God in 1936. K. E. Abraham, once Cook's associate, left in 1930 to found what became the Indian Pentecostal Church of God.
Indian arm of the Church of God (Cleveland)
Separate structures for Kerala and other regions
Strong among Dalit Christians of central Travancore
Scripture with the Church of God Declaration of Faith.
Justification, sanctification and Spirit baptism evidenced by tongues.
Baptism by immersion, Lord's Supper and footwashing.
Episcopal-style overseers appointed within the Church of God structure.
Pentecostal worship in Malayalam and other languages.
traditions/assemblies-of-god-india/summa: The Indian fellowship of the Assemblies of God, rooted in missionary work from 1915–16 and formally organised in 1918, with Christian H. Schoonmaker as founding chairman. Bethel Bible College in Punalur, Kerala (1927), was the first permanent Assemblies of God Bible school outside the United States. Its General Council, headquartered in Chennai, was formed in 1995 and joins regional councils such as the South India Assemblies of God.
traditions/assemblies-of-god-india/disti: Indian member of the World Assemblies of God Fellowship
Regional district councils for Kerala, Tamil Nadu and North India
Large urban congregations such as New Life Assembly of God, Chennai
traditions/assemblies-of-god-india/profi: Scripture with the Assemblies of God Statement of Fundamental Truths.
Salvation by grace through faith; Spirit baptism evidenced by tongues.
Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper as ordinances.
Cooperative fellowship: autonomous churches in district councils under a General Council.
Contemporary and traditional Pentecostal worship in many languages.
